segments.text: Oh,
25 years ago, Narendra Modi was a political organizer, not an elected politician.
Now he is completing 25 years as the serving head of an elected government in India, first in Gujarat and now in Delhi.
The journey began in Gujarat in October 2001 at a moment when the BJP was battling political instability.
Keshubhai Patel's government was under pressure and the state was still dealing with the devastation of the Bhuj earthquake.
Modi had never contested an election.
He had never run a government.
Yet the BJP's central leadership took the extraordinary decision to send its organizational man from Delhi to Gandhinagar and make him the Gujarat Chief Minister.
So what happened behind the scenes?
Why Modi?
Who pushed his name?

What did Atal Bihari Vajpayee and LK Advani make of the choice and was that decision seen then as a temporary political fix or did some people already recognize something much bigger in Narendra Modi?

Well, to understand that call that changed everything in 2001, I am now joined by veteran journalist Uday Mahurkarji, who was reporting on Modi at that time and has followed his political journey for decades.

Mahurka Ji, 2001, that famous India Today profile he wrote described Mr. Modi as an unusual exception within the RSS tradition and RSS pracharag, becoming a chief minister while remaining a full-time organizational worker.
So, Uday Ji, take us back to that October 2001 days.
Why do you think the BJP took that call?
Was it instability?
Was it the government wheeling from the earthquake?
Or do you think there was something more to it?
Difficult to answer, but all three, I would say.
The BJP had lost the civic elections, state civic elections.
That was instability part.
Earthquake, of course, there were many issues which needed to be dealt with properly.
And third, Narendra Modi, I think, was never seen as a stop-gap arrangement.
And one thing I must put here very
strongly.
You see, a good organizer can always be a good administrator.
This dichotomy being seen between the two, I don't think it is justified.
He was an organizer par excellence.
He was a visionary person.
He had resolution, men of strong resolution.
Correct?
Understood politics, understood public life.
I remember once when he was
We had a commissioner called Mr. Verma.
He was trying to remove encroachments and there was a big agitation against him in the dead of the night.
He took the liberty of calling up Mr. Modi at 1.30 in the night.
Mr. Modi, I am doing such a good job and your party workers are not allowing me to do it.
Mr. Modi got into his car, went there and ensured that those encroachments were removed.
This was dynamism, you know.
You don't find it everywhere.
So when he was brought, I think he was brought with the understanding that he will do a good job even on the long run.
Absolutely.
And you know, Narendra Modi sir had never fought an election till then.
He had never run a government.
So why was he considered the answer?
What did the BJP leadership, do you think, saw in him that you believe would compensate for the lack of, I would say, administrative experience?
Let me tell you one thing.
When Mr. Modi was the Sanghathan Mantri of Gujarat BJP, at that time, in 1991, he was a member of the Central Election Committee.
So his talent, his vision, his way of working, his way of looking at problems of this nation were quite known to all the leaders, including Advani ji.
It was a very rare thing for a state organizational secretary to become a member of the central election committee in which there are only 11 members.
So he had that spark.
I have no doubt.
So, his success is not something which has come out of the blue, you know.
I mean, he is a person, if you give him a task, he will do 99% a good job.
Correct?
Do you think Mr. Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Mr. L.K.
Advani had this opinion about Narendra Modi at that time?
I think Mr. Vajpayee was not so much in favour as Mr. Advani.
But Mr. Advani convinced Mr. Vajpayee.
And even RSS was convinced, you know.
Do you think some of it also came from the RSS?
You see, I'll tell you one thing.
You know the 1995 episode when Shankar Singh of Agela rebelled against the BJP leadership, particularly against Mr. Modi.
Yes.
That rebellion was seen against Keshavbhai Patel.
It was more against Narendra Modi.
And he was banished from Gujarat and he was sent to Delhi.
That became a blazing and disguise for him.
He developed relations here.
People came to know about his abilities.
I remember he was in charge of Haryana when BJP and Bansilal's party, they were in power in Haryana.
And that time, he had done a wonderful job of seeing that as a party in charge, he leaves an impact on the governance also.
He had a very good understanding with Bansilal.
It was like Modiji says, aapda mein aafsar.
Toh Gujraj se bhej diya, Delhi.
But Delhi aakar unhone apna ek neya soroop mein aa gaya.
Bilkul.
Chikki unmein spark thi na.
Dikho, Kargil war hua jab.
So, ek party ka view tha ho bahut achchi thare nahi aa raha tha public ke beech mein.
Narendra bhai ko draft kiya gaya.
And the moment he started addressing press conference every day during the Kargil war, I mean,
He was able to put forward the party's view very well, nation's view very well before the people.
Because he has a very strong command over Gujarati, Hindi.
Correct?
My mother used to always ask me, how come he is a Gujarati?
How does he speak such good Hindi?
You see, one thing you have to understand.
Look, I always, for myself, I used to say with pride, you know, that I never tell a story without going on the spot.
In my 40 years of career as a journalist, I have only told two or three stories without going on the spot.
So, Mr. Modi was always there at the spot when things were happening.
Secondly, very few people know, people think that
Yatra as a political tool is a creation of some other leader, Pramod Mahajan so to say.
I think Mr. Modi is the person who invented this political tool in Gujarat.
There was drought in Gujarat in 1987 when he was the organization secretary.
I met him in 1987 only for the first time and he said that
and the anti-doubt measures were not very good.
Congress government was in power at that time.
He made a strategy where four Nyaya Yatra were started, led by Shankar Singh Bhagila.
Justice was a doubt affected.
See, Yatra is a tool.
I very strongly think it is Modi who invented that.
Yatra has become a tool of Indian politics.
It is a way of expressing people's wish, people's desires.
It is a tool for expressing lack of governance.
And nationalism of Mr. Modi, as you have known him from 1987, so almost 40 years, it's a very long journey, almost four decades.

Nationalism is something which is central to the philosophy of Mr. Narendra Modi, even if we see during the emergency days what he has done, or be it that Tiranga Yatra to Srinagar to hoist the flag at Lalchowk.
that continues till day.
Do you think that's also a strong factor which may have influenced Mr. Vajpayee, Mr. Advani, that this is a man.
We need at the centre of the BJP as a Chief Minister to ensure our agenda also or nationalism is reinforced.
And he has lived up to the reputation.
Let me share with you here and with the nation that this menace of bombings by terrorists, ultra-Wahhabi terrorists, by Indian Mujahideen,
other bodies.
This stopped only because of Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah.
You recall the period between 2004 and 2010, series of blasts across the country Bangalore, Pune, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Jaipur.
When did it stop?
When they committed the blunder
of doing serial blasts in Gujarat, that was a point that they played into the wrong hands.
Who?
The terrorists.
I think Gujarat's real blasts were on 26 July, 2008.
And within 21 days, they could get the clue.
And since the BJ government was not compromised,
Not that Congress governments were totally compromised.
But there was pressure of Wahhabi elements on the government, you know.
That pressure, it was free, you know.
So it caught hold of the links of terrorists across the country.
And that's all, if you see, if you leave aside the Mumbai blasts which were directly engineered by Pakistan, you know.
There was no blasts after that for many, many years.
The reason is Narendra Modi and his government.
When they got the first clue, there was a Maulavi, Bashir, I think.
Bashir.
He was in, I think, Azamgarh.
And he had to be brought to Ahmedabad immediately.
Mr. Modi sent his own plane.
The officers went in his plane.
And then there was an attempt of, I don't know which government was there, to stop it.
But they managed to bring him on the same day.
That was the first clue to the serial blast and which were linked to other blasts in the country.
Because the module was same, Indian Mojaheddin, which is members of former CME.
I remember Mr. Modi saying, because the challenge as soon as he became the Chief Minister also came in 2002.
I remember him saying in one of the interviews that when the Sabarmati Express incident happened, some of my officers said, don't go there.
But he said, no, I will go there.
And he himself went there and saw what had happened.
What do you think of Mr. Modi's handling of 2002?
Because that's something that he's many a time attacked.
I will tell you one.
This was the first incident of that sort.
I'm talking about the Godhra incident.
Yes.
a mob of Muslims burned down 59 Hindus to death.
This was the first such incident in India after the onset of the TV Yug, electronic media era, you know.
Electronic media era starts from 1998, if you remember, when the Vajpayee government allowed private channels to come.
Correct?
So, there was a big reaction against the Muslim community.
Mr. Modi tried his level best.
I am telling you, there are three incidents I have covered.
Had the Gujarat police not intervened, if you join these three incidents, 8,000 Muslims would have died.
Their lives were saved by Gujarat police under Mr. Modi.
One was at Sanjeli in Panchmahal district, not very far from Godhra.
Another was at Bodeli, which is again about 80 kilometers from Godhra.
And third was in Bhawanagar, where a crowd of 10,000 Hindus attacked the Madrasa, from where a boy had slipped out and joined a Pakistani movement.
And he was killed by Indian forces on the Indo-Pak border.
He was a Kashmiri studying in that madrasa in Bhavnagar.
Now at all these three places it was Gujarat police who saved the lives of the Muslims.
In Sanjali about 2500 people, in Bodili again they are all refugees, in Bodili again 2500 people, 8000
bow, arrow and bow-wielding adivasis and gun-wielding adivasis were there to kill.
Police fired.
I think two or three people died in that firing.
So, Mr. Modi's handling was quite good.
He sought army.
He sought help from Congress governments.
He sought police help, police, additional police from Congress which was not given to him.
Correct?
But then it was a mass movement against Muslim community which was to an extent uncontrollable.
You see, if you look at the FIRs lodged between in the first three days of the riots, correct?
If you look at the numbers mentioned of the mobs, then 30 lakh Hindus were on the road in central Gujarat targeting Muslims.
The strength of police in
Gujarat police, including reserve police, was only 70,000.
So, you have to understand that.
I will take a year back to the case.
And thereafter, if you read my story of 2010, inhuman rights, I have proved that many of these cases were false.
The Muslim witnesses themselves told me that human rights activists came to us
They asked us to sign on a paper and we did, we do not know what was there in the paper.
So, while there was a failure on the part of the government, administrative failure, but there was no intent.
It is what I feel.
Very important.
And sir, how important was, I would say, the 2002 Gujarat assembly election in transforming Mr. Modi from what many said appointed chief minister to an elected chief minister?
Of course, he's never seen back since then.
He's never lost an election since then.
In fact, was 2001 the moment he was given power?
But was 2002 the moment that he established, I would say, his own political mandate?
Absolutely.
I will tell you, unfortunately, what happened.
the pressure which was mounted by the human rights activists against Mr. Modi amongst the people as well as within the BJP.
Even Mr. Vajpayee at that point felt that Mr. Modi might be a liability.
Nobody will talk about it openly, but I am telling you.
Correct?
So he started that Gujarat Gaurav Yatra.
Correct?
He did 10 rounds of Gujarat, that Gujarat Gaurav Yatra.
I was there with him in 8 or 9 rounds.
You know, there used to be Rath, DCM to Oita, correct?
The driver used to be on this side, on the other window used to be Mr. Modi and I used to sit in between on a stool.
So, I saw that entire Yatra.
At the very first place called Vijapur, this was started I think in September.
at the very first place called Vijapur, where the first stop was there.
The crowd was maybe 1000 people, you know.
But what ladies started doing, they started lifting their children and telling Mr. Modi to bless their child.
He was being seen as a protector and this continued.
I am talking about the first round.
This continued throughout this and then I called up one of my editors at that time was Mr. Swapan Dasgupta.
He was the number two.
I called him up and told him, whenever the elections are held, I don't think anybody can defeat him.
This whole phenomena of mothers lifting their children and telling Mr. Modi to bless him, this continued throughout that Garav Yatra.
Very interesting.

And Udayji was just telling me before this interview, in fact, that Mr. Modi's transformation also from a Hindi-speaking, Gujarati-speaking chief minister to now what we see him, a global leader, I would say.
Like learning English, you were telling me a small anecdote.
What happened about that?
It's slightly personal, but now so many years have passed.
And I think it shows his ability also.
I told you, he's a man of resolution.
In 2000, he went to Staten Island, where Mr. Vajpayee had gone.
And there he gave an interview in English, in a broken English, you know.
So when he came back, I told him, I said, Mr. Dhanendra, this country is a very strange country.
If you don't speak the native language properly, no one will read it.
But if you don't speak English properly, people will beat you.
He just listened to me.
In 2004, as chief minister, again he spoke something in English, and which was, again, broken, you know.
So again I told him.
He said, no.
your advice is wrong.
In India, if I want to succeed in public life, then English is a language which I should know.
And this is the only way I will be able to learn this language.
And suddenly I found in 2008, he had gone to Chennai to address one function with Jayalalitha.
And there he spoke in English for almost, I think, half an hour or so.
And in the night when he came, when I spoke to him on phone, he told me that today I have delivered my first lecture in English.
It went fairly well.
And thereafter, when I saw him speaking English, there was sudden improvement.
Now what he had done, I don't know.
I remember one interview he gave on winning the 2012 assembly election to Rajdeep Sardesai.
It was the first time I felt that he has
learned the language well.
Short sentences, very clear, no mistake.
That's how quickly Mr. Modi also adapts and learns.
He's a man of resolution.
He's a man of resolution.
How he has tackled this whole issue.
For the first four or five years as Prime Minister, he used to speak in English.
Now he has come down to Hindi.
Now he's moving to Gen Z, sir.
Now he's saying, hey, friends.
Earlier, brothers and sisters.
Now Mr. Modi says, hey, friends.
He's a very fast learner.
What do you think of his latest, you know, Instagram, you know, he's going to Instagram, making these short reels also, you know, a man who's 75 plus.
I mean, this shows his ability to change himself according to the situation.
I think we must salute him for this.
At this age,

Mind you one thing, there is criticism of him in the recent months and years on certain aspects of his governance, particularly overuse of ED and CBI against opposition only, taking apportioned leader inside the party, closing cases against them.
I think this politics has affected even party's image badly, I think.
But on the other hand, he has done a wonderful job.
You see, there is not a single area of governance, almost, virtually, where India has not registered two-fold progress or many-fold in the last 12 years as compared to the preceding 60 years.
It's not a small record.
One more thing I want to clarify here.
There have been many incidents where infrastructure projects
after being launched, have seen something, you know, there is a hole, water is falling.
Let me tell you one thing, of course, this is of course because of lack of monitoring.
But one thing you have to understand, you see, the problem with this government is, it wants to do things
as fast as possible.
So, if a project has to take four years, it has to take four years.
The contractor will be told you do it in three years, do it in two years.
That is the reason.
People are linking it to corruption.
Absolutely wrong.
It is not an issue of corruption.
It is an issue of forcing the contractors to finish the project before the deadline, much before the deadline.

In fact, in the recent Pragati meeting that the PM held a few weeks back, he in fact said that, you know, it's important that project should not go time and cost overruns, but also quality is important.
So should I put fourth party quality audits now, the Prime Minister said.
It is driven by that.
But then a lot of people have linked this to corruption.
Yes.
So somebody told me this is 40% corruption.
All nonsense.
Money in the scheme of Mr. Modi is not a high priority thing.
Not that it doesn't manage funds, but it will not manage funds at the cost of quality of road and quality of airport.
It is happening because of some poor monitoring and two, this setting deadlines which are impossible to meet.
Run up to 2014, I would like to ask you this second last question.
At what point did you see that personally realize that the Gujarat experiment with Mr. Modi had become a national political model?
What was the point you thought that Mr. Modi is now ready to become Prime Minister?
I said it in not in so many words in 2010.
I have written that Mr. Modi has mounted his challenge for the prime ministership.
This I have written in 2010.
You were the first one to write this.
I think I was the first person.
You see, I could see that he has got vision.
There is controversy going on about Raghuraj, former RBI governor.
Correct?
Now, in that,
I read this.
He is giving credit for UPI to UPA government.
Yes, partially it is true.
It is UPA government which came up with this idea.
But who made it possible?
There are no bank accounts in the country.
It was Mr. Modi.
Only 58 crore people had bank accounts in the country when he took over.
Get my point?
So, the credit must go to Mr. Modi, not UPA government.
And I am telling you one thing, today there is a lot of criticism of this government in many quarters.
Some would misplace, some of it is justified.
But just imagine, had this government not come in 2014, what would have happened?
Previous government was totally sold out to Wahhabi elements.
Let us start with national security.
Zakir Naik had full support from behind the screen when the UPA was in power, hate preacher Zakir Naik.
Correct?
I mean the ultra Wahhabi elements which are in Devbhant, correct?
They and government were in full, you know, I mean, they were working in tandem.
This Hindu terror thing in 2008, whatever that is.
So, let us start with national security.
Bringing down the menace of Naxalism, moist menace from 100 districts to just one or two or three districts, it's not a small achievement.
It's not a big achievement.
So nations should ponder, you know, long term removal of 370.
Yes.
It's a big, you know, if you look at history, after Islam came to Indian subcontinent, once Marathas captured Peshawar in 1758 for six months.
And after Ranji Singh captured Peshawar for few.
Otherwise, for 1000 years,
for the first time in Kashmir and just see the progress.
Ranji Trophy team of Kashmir, mixed team of Hindus and Muslims, they have won Ranji Trophy this year.
Absolutely.
It's not a small thing.
When Pahelgaon happened, people look at it very differently.
Some of our people in the sense, the right-wingers, ultra-right-wingers, they think that they were involved in this.
If two Pune people were involved, then 25 Pune people were helping the victims.
Absolutely.
You can't ignore that.
It's a big achievement in the way the Muslims came out against Pakistan after Pehelgaum.
Even if you think that some of them were doing Altakia, Altakia is after-fuge, showing something else and doing something else.
Correct?
Even if you take Altakia part also, I think 50% were genuine protesters against Pakistan, which has never happened in Kashmir.
Kashmir in fact is a big success story I would say of Mr. Modi and Uday Mahurkar Ji giving us very interesting insights into Mr. Modi's life and his whole journey.
